title: Minimum Limit of Balls in a Bag
summary: Given an array of integers representing the number of balls in each bag and a maximum number of operations, you can split any bag into two new bags at most that many times.
statement: Given an array of integers representing the number of balls in each bag and a maximum number of operations, you can split any bag into two new bags at most that many times. The goal is to minimize the maximum number of balls in any bag after the operations. Return the smallest possible maximum number of balls in a bag.
constraints: One operation splits a bag into two positive-sized bags.
Minimize the maximum balls in any bag using at most max_operations splits.
reference_solution:
def minimum_bag_penalty(nums, max_operations):
 low,high=1,max(nums)
 while low<high:
  middle=(low+high)//2
  if sum((value-1)//middle for value in nums)<=max_operations:high=middle
  else:low=middle+1
 return low

hints: For a proposed limit p, a bag of size x needs floor((x-1)/p) splits.
Feasibility is monotone, so binary-search the smallest feasible penalty.
Sum required splits at each midpoint; move high down when within budget, otherwise low to midpoint+1.
Larger limits never require more splits, and the formula is the minimum pieces needed to keep every part at most p.

tests.explanation: Splitting nine into three bags of three uses two operations, so the minimum penalty is three.
Penalty two is achievable in four splits and penalty one is not.
